solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Outlaw supporting writer

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A scribe on the side of a bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: To proscribe something is to forbid or ban it, the verb sense of outlaw.

clue.text: It's dreadful ascending hill — number will stay at bottom

indicators.note: in a down entry the number's letters sit beneath the rest, so they come last
in a down clue, ascending means the word for hill is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common in Devon place names
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A grumble that it is awful to climb a hill while a figure stays down at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten is informal for very bad or awful, a synonym of dreadful.

clue.text: Supper's beginning with fish smell

indicators.note: beginning asks for the opening letter of the word Supper's

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Dinner starts with fish, and the kitchen reeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong unpleasant odour, a synonym for a bad smell.

clue.text: Issue that troubles Ulster

indicators.note: troubles means stirs up or disturbs, so the letters of Ulster are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political matter causing unrest in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Troubles was the name for the decades of conflict in Northern Ireland (Ulster), which makes the surface very natural.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is an outcome or consequence, which is a synonym of result.

clue.text: Torrent of anger in the pub?

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the counter in one
rage is fury, strong anger

explanation.surface: A flood of fury breaking out in a public house.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works like road rage: fury that breaks out among drinkers, with the drinking place first.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy, continuous outpouring, as in a barrage of questions, like a torrent.

clue.text: Anger against topsy-turvy board is genuine

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, so in a down clue the pair before it is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger
v is short for versus, against
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Fury at an upended board game is real enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topsy-turvy' flips the anger-and-against pair as one unit, giving VERI; the board follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Veritable means real or true to name, a synonym for genuine.

clue.text: Open cut bled too much?

parts.note: overt means done openly, not hidden
axed means cut, chopped

explanation.surface: Asks whether an open wound bled excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bled' is not about blood: to bleed someone is to extract money from them, and taxing too heavily does that; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overtaxed is to be charged too heavily, figuratively drained of money, as a bled patient loses blood.

clue.text: Bus blocking us out where it's parked? Verbal abuse results

indicators.note: out says the letters of us are removed from the word Bus

parts.note: the obstructing bus of the surface supplies just the word bus
taken as written
a bus may be parked at the roadside, the edge of a road

explanation.surface: A bus left obstructing the road prompts a stream of insults from drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' only paints the bus in the way; once us is out, its B stands in front of the roadside, as a parked bus would.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadside is a fierce verbal attack, from the firing of all a ship's guns on one side.

clue.text: Drowning in drink is a very small animal

indicators.note: drowning in means the pieces before it sit submerged inside the drink

parts.note: beer is a drink
very abbreviates to v, written small as a lowercase letter

explanation.surface: A tiny creature has fallen into someone's pint.
explanation.definitionFit: The beaver is a large dam-building rodent, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Terribly late, one certain to be taking one's time

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of late are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone sure of themselves strolls in very late, unhurried.
explanation.definitionFit: At leisure describes acting without hurry, an idiom for taking one's time.

clue.text: Knight hiding hesitation when approaching a mountain range

indicators.note: approaching means coming up to, so the A follows
hiding means the knight's title holds the hesitation within it

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A knight conceals his doubts as he nears some peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains, especially in Spain or the Americas.

clue.text: The female copper — thin or big and strong?

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
lean means thin

explanation.surface: Asks whether a policewoman is slight or powerfully built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Herculean means having the enormous strength of the Greek hero Hercules, so mighty and muscular.

clue.text: Heathens making vessels with silver lining

indicators.note: a lining sits inside, so the silver goes within the vessels

parts.note: pans are cooking vessels
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Unbelievers crafting pots with silver insides.
explanation.definitionFit: Pagans are followers of a non-mainstream or polytheistic religion, historically called heathens.

clue.text: Writer of dramatic script needing exceptional actress in

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A screenplay calls for an outstanding actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenarist writes screenplays or scenarios for films and plays.

clue.text: Little fellow trapped in house expresses scorn for medical facilities

indicators.note: trapped in means the fellow is enclosed by the scornful word

parts.note: to spit is to show contempt
Al is a short form of a man's name such as Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A small man shut up at home sneers at clinics.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals are institutions where the sick are treated, the chief medical facilities.

clue.text: Specially financed party set up and getting on

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the party word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party
getting on means growing old, aged

explanation.surface: An ageing group of revellers raises money in a special way.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveraged deal is funded largely with borrowed money, a particular kind of financing.

clue.text: Cut not all of the wood

indicators.note: not all of means only some consecutive letters of the words are used

explanation.surface: Fell only some of the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop or cut with an axe, a synonym.

clue.text: Have to spend pounds for builder's item

indicators.note: to spend means to pay out, so the pounds sign leaves the word

parts.note: to hold is to have or possess
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Having to pay money for a building supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A hod is a builder's open trough on a pole for carrying bricks.

clue.text: Question of puzzlement from character becoming audible

indicators.note: becoming audible means the letter's spoken sound is what counts

parts.note: a character is a letter, here the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud about a character in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Why is the word asking for a reason, the typical utterance of a puzzled person.

clue.text: Near wild ocelots

indicators.note: wild signals the letters are rearranged freely

explanation.surface: A warning that untamed big cats are nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to is a phrase meaning at a short distance from, so nearby.

clue.text: Henry, king presumably resting old weapon

parts.note: Hal is a pet name for Henry, as Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: presumably invites the picture of a king lying down, so his letter goes inside the place of rest

parts.note: resting suggests lying in bed
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Henry the monarch, apparently at rest, with an antique arm.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is pictured resting in BED, so R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a medieval combined spear and battleaxe on a long pole.

clue.text: Precise removal of article from cart

indicators.note: removal of means the article's letter is taken away

parts.note: a dray is a low heavy cart for brewers' barrels
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Exactly how you take an item off a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry can mean matter-of-fact or exact, as dry facts, close to precise.

clue.text: Managed to talk at length in Asian city

parts.note: ran means managed, as ran a business
to go on is to talk on and on

explanation.surface: Someone coped with chattering for ages in an Asian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon is the former name of Yangon, the largest city of Myanmar.

clue.text: Youngster is very quiet when external control is brought back

indicators.note: external means the control word lies outside the quiet sign
brought back means the word for control is reversed

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse, so control
pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: A child goes silent once discipline from outside returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is a British informal word for a small child.

clue.text: Wise person's spoken with energy about origin of capitalism

indicators.note: about means the spoken word and energy surround the next letter

parts.note: oral means spoken

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of capitalism

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A sage talks energetically on how capitalism began.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person thought to give wise authoritative counsel, like a sage.

clue.text: Dropout having year off with huge animals in the wild

indicators.note: off means the year letter is taken away

parts.note: a hippy is someone who dropped out of conventional society
OS is short for outsize, huge

explanation.surface: A gap-year dropout goes on safari among enormous beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippos are hippopotamuses, large African mammals seen in rivers in the wild.

clue.text: Writer with name on flag

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a writer

explanation.surface: An author signs a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow triangular flag, as on a lance.

clue.text: Lacking discipline, silly nude catches puff-puff

indicators.note: catches means the jumbled word wraps round the other piece
silly signals the letters of nude are scrambled

parts.note: puff-puff is a nursery word for a steam train

explanation.surface: A foolish naked person boards a train, behaving wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrained means not taught or drilled, so lacking discipline.

clue.text: Customary practice of Spiritualists

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A habit of spiritualists at séances.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a ceremony or habitual routine regularly performed, a customary practice.

clue.text: Rodent in yellow vessel hidden in wood

indicators.note: hidden in means the yellow vessel is placed inside the wood

parts.note: pine is a wood
or is gold or yellow in heraldry
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A rodent inside a golden pot concealed in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: The porcupine is a rodent with sharp defensive quills.

clue.text: Church book, we hear, is one for preservation

indicators.note: we hear signals that the church book is only spoken, its silent P dropped

parts.note: a psalter is a book of psalms used in church

explanation.surface: A hymnal is said to keep things safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A salter is someone who preserves food with salt, one who works at preserving.

clue.text: Never giving up in ascents proving tricky

indicators.note: proving tricky suggests the letters are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: Relentless when climbs get difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Incessant means continuing without pause, never letting up.
